label: conj:binding-manybody-eq-jet-filtration
title: Binding many-body series equals the jet-order filtration: $B(K)=\sum_n m_e\,a_D^{(n)}$
html:
Conjecture. Binding many-body series equals the jet-order filtration: B(K)=\sum_n m_e\,a_D^{(n)}

Conjecture (binding many-body series = jet-order filtration).

The per-isotope binding energy of the canonical braid \mathcal{B}_K is the body-order series

B(K) \;=\; \sum_{n \geq 2} B_n(K),
\qquad
B_n(K) \;=\; m_e\,a_D^{(n)}(K)
\;=\; m_e\oint_{\mathcal{S}_c}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)}
\;=\; m_e\,2\pi i\!\!\sum_{p\,\in\,\mathcal{S}_c^{\mathrm{hyp}}}\!\!
        \mathrm{Res}_p\,\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)},

in which the body order n is the vertical (jet) degree of the prolonged Seiberg--Witten differential (prop:mi-sw-abelianisation), the n-body term is m_e times the n-th prolonged SW period, and that period is the algebraic residue sum of prop:sw-period-residue-sum taken over the hyperbolic components only (non-hyperbolic components contribute \mathrm{Vol}=0). Equivalently: the many-body binding series coincides with the jet-order filtration of \mathcal{B}_K, term by term.

The growth of the residue weights with body order — the empirical "\rho\cdot A" scale rule — is conjectured to be the solution of a q-difference equation on the binding generating function G(x;q)=\sum_n B_n x^n, namely G(qx;q)=R(q,x)\,G(x;q), whose Archimedean (\tau) image is a Dirac-type partial differential equation. Under this conjecture \rho\cdot A is an output of the recursion, not a fitted constant.

Anchors. The series is referred to two body orders: the n=2 deuteron term (single inter-nucleon bond) and the n=4 magic-shell term magic-A-binding-formula, B(^{4}\mathrm{He}) = \rho_F\,m_e\,A\,\mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{L6a4}) with \rho_F = 2, which lands ^{4}\mathrm{He} within +5.87\%. The conjecture asserts that these are the n=2 and n=4 members of one filtration, with the n=3 term the genuine three-body contribution (not reducible to pairwise sums).

What the two anchors do and do not pin. Read with the weight w_n of the scope note below, the unknowns through A=4 are w_2,w_3,w_4 — three — against two anchor equations, so one free parameter survives and the n=3 term is not determined. The n=2 anchor fixes w_2; the n=4 anchor is a single equation in the two remaining unknowns, so for every w_3 there is exactly one w_4 = (B_{\mathrm{magic}}/m_e - a_D^{(2)}w_2 - a_D^{(3)}w_3)/a_D^{(4)} holding both anchors identically. The A=3 prediction along that family, B(^{3}\mathrm{H}) = m_e(a_D^{(2)}w_2 + a_D^{(3)}w_3), is unbounded in w_3, so A=3 cannot test the n=3 term — it defines it. Adding positivity and monotone growth w_2 \leq w_3 \leq w_4 narrows the induced B(^{3}\mathrm{H}) to a window 66–78\% of the observable's own magnitude, which the data does satisfy; that consistency is the one non-circular check the anchors support, and it carries that width. The count is unchanged if the n=4 anchor is instead read as pinning the n=4 term alone, since nothing then mentions w_3 at all.

Neither anchor is parameter-free as stated. The prefactor \rho_F = 2 is consumed as an input hypothesis, not derived — see the doubly-magic binding context. And the w_2 = 4.353 used across the w_n probes is B_{\mathrm{AME}}(^{2}\mathrm{H}) inverted, an extraction; the derived single p–n bond gives \alpha L_{pn} \approx 2.833\ \mathrm{MeV}, +27.3\% above the measured 2.2246\ \mathrm{MeV}, hence w_2 \approx 5.544 instead. Rigidity for w_3 would have to come from the derived kernel R(q,x), which is open. Measured in binding_n3_forcing_probe.py; scope-(a) analysis in the n=3 forcing audit.

This is an open conjecture: the residue-sum form of each term is established and the two anchors are stated, but the anchors are conditional in the sense just described, they leave the n=3 term free, and the equality of the full binding to the complete jet-order filtration — together with the q-difference origin of the scale rule — is not proved.

Scope note on the weight w_n(K). A derive-or-refute probe of the weight kernel establishes what does not close. Body-order weights w_n (shared across knots K) are admissible: the raw ^{3}\mathrm{H}/^{3}\mathrm{He} binding split (0.76\ \text{MeV}, 9.9\%) is almost entirely Coulomb — on the Coulomb-corrected strong binding B_{\mathrm{strong}} the mirror pair agrees to \sim 2.7\% (charge-symmetry breaking), so a K-independent w_n is not excluded. That 2.7\% is geometry-dependent: at the canonical derived r_0 = \hbar c/m_\pi of coulomb_energy.py the correction overshoots and the residual is \approx -1\% with ^{3}\mathrm{He} the more bound partner, while the measured-charge-radius geometry gives +1\%; the spread across geometries is 0.16\ \mathrm{MeV}, which does not affect the admissibility conclusion. But no parameter-free constant-ratio kernel R(q,n) reproduces the extracted w_2,w_3,w_4 to 5\% (geometric 22.7\%, [n]_q 29.4\%, [n]_q^2 6.9\% the lone near-miss), and a tuned recursion is the banned seventh \Delta_\lambda ansatz. A fully K-dependent kernel is underdetermined by the anchors (A-1 unknowns against one equation per isotope) — extraction is a fit. Closure therefore requires the derived R(q,x). The eigenfunction relation of the na-Stokes period a_D^{(n)}=S(n)/n (the seed c_3=[2]_q exact, and the Habiro (q-1)^2\Phi_3 deviation, formalized in QOU.Mass.BindingEigenfunctionTwoTier) supplies a derived target for R(q,x) but does not determine it — the binding deviation and the Q_\beta c_k ladder share the Habiro ring, not the same element.

How much is undetermined, exactly, and why no scalar R(q,x) can supply it. "Does not determine it" is now a count rather than a caution. With R an unconstrained formal power series the shift relation determines exactly one kernel coefficient per body order, and conversely: for any body sequence with B_2 \neq 0 the map \{r_k\} \leftrightarrow \{B_n\} is a bijection (QOU.Mass.BindingScalarKernelParityExclusion.kernel_coeff_existsUnique, sorry-free). So the unconstrained ansatz constrains nothing: it reparametrises the unknown weights, it does not remove them, and "\rho\cdot A is an output of the recursion" is false unless R is independently pinned. All of the ansatz's content therefore lies in the finiteness of the Laurent window.

That finiteness is unattainable in the scalar form. The q-Borel-normalized carrier is the rank-2 module \mathcal{K} of conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol, which is irreducible — its Newton slope \tfrac12 is not an integer, while every rank-1 q-difference module has integer slope — so no scalar R(q,x)\in K(x) acts on it at all, at any depth. The kernel that closes this conjecture must be a 2\times2 matrix, and a rank-2 recursion needs two base cases, so the n=3 term is required as an independent input rather than produced by the recursion. This is consistent with, and independent of, the one-free-parameter count recorded above.

A multi-anchor test (D\to{}^{12}C, Coulomb-corrected) further shows that the full-tower reading — summing B(K)=\sum_{n=2}^{A} m_e\,a_D^{(n)}\,w_n to the nucleon count A — is refuted for A\geq 5: the na-Stokes period a_D^{(n)} grows super-exponentially while B/A\to\mathrm{const}, so any bounded or amplifying body-order weight overshoots (\sim{+}920\% at {}^{6}Li, \sim{+}2\times10^{6}\% at {}^{12}C). The series must therefore be a few-body truncation (fixed small n_{\max}, a 2–3-body cluster count \times A-multiplicity, matching nuclear 2-/3-body force dominance), not a sum to A; the na-Stokes period remains the correct light-nucleus (A\leq 4) kernel.
